mainTopic: The practical differences between רבי יוחנן and רבי חנינא about which details of the מילואים are essential, with proofs that each detail is not essential לדורות, and the source for the stricter view.
overview: On the previous amud, רבי יוחנן and רבי חנינא disagreed about the מילואים, the seven-day inauguration of the כהנים. One view says כל הכתוב בהן מעכב בהן: every detail written there is essential. The other says דבר שאין מעכב לדורות אין מעכב בהן: a detail that is not essential for regular קרבנות later on is not essential in the מילואים either. The גמרא now asks what practical difference this makes. Four אמוראים each give an example. רב יוסף says סמיכה, רב נחמן בר יצחק says תנופה, רב פפא says פרישת שבעה, and רבינא says seven days of ריבוי and משיחה. For each example, the גמרא proves that it is not essential לדורות. For סמיכה and תנופה it uses ברייתות that end 'כאילו לא כפר, וכפר'. For פרישת שבעה it relies on the משנה's word מתקינין. For ריבוי and משיחה it uses a ברייתא that says 'מכל מקום'. The גמרא then finds a source that seven days of משיחה is still required לכתחילה. Finally, רבי יצחק בר ביסנא explains the stricter view from the word ״כָּכָה״, and the גמרא begins a challenge to that source that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב יוסף: The difference is placing hands
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the two opinions disagree about סמיכה. Under כל הכתוב בהן מעכב, skipping סמיכה invalidates the מילואים. Under the other view, it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Placing hands is the difference between them. According to the one who says everything written about them is essential, placing hands is essential. According to the one who says that whatever is not essential for later generations is not essential for them, placing hands is not essential.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the open question of what practical difference exists between the two opinions about the מילואים. His answer is סמיכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סמיכה is written in the מילואים section, so the view that 'everything written is essential' would require it. But סמיכה is not essential for regular קרבנות in later generations. So the view that 'what is not essential later is not essential here' would not require it. That makes סמיכה a clear case where the two views split.

steps.title: How do we know placing hands is not essential for regular offerings?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that סמיכה does not invalidate regular קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for later generations, how do we know that placing hands is not essential?

steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's answer only works if סמיכה is truly not essential for regular קרבנות. If it were essential, both opinions would agree it is essential in the מילואים, and there would be no difference. So the גמרא wants a source.

steps.title: ברייתא: Can placing hands bring atonement?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes 'וסמך... ונרצה' and asks how סמיכה could bring atonement, since only the blood atones.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'And he shall place his hand... and it shall be accepted.' Does placing hands bring atonement? Isn't atonement only through the blood, as it says: 'For it is the blood that atones for the soul'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as its proof. The ברייתא starts by raising a problem with how the פסוק is phrased.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק places 'וסמך' (he shall place hands) right next to 'ונרצה' (it shall be accepted). That makes it sound as if סמיכה itself brings כפרה. But another פסוק says that only the blood atones. So the ברייתא sets up a puzzle, and solving it will show what role סמיכה really plays.

keyTerms.meaning: And it shall be accepted (for atonement)
Atonement
But does...? (a rhetorical challenge)

steps.title: Skipping placing hands: atonement still happens
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that someone who treats סמיכה as a minor leftover is viewed as if he did not atone. Even so, he did atone.
steps.simpleTranslation: So why does the verse say 'and he shall place... and it shall be accepted'? To teach that if he treated placing hands as a leftover part of the מצוה, the verse considers him as if he did not atone. Yet he did atone!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא solves its own puzzle. That solution is the proof that skipping סמיכה does not invalidate a regular קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links סמיכה to כפרה to show that סמיכה is important, not to make it essential. Without it, the כפרה is incomplete ('as if he did not atone'), yet real atonement still happens ('וכפר'). So for regular קרבנות, סמיכה is not essential, which is exactly what רב יוסף needed.

steps.whatToRemember: For regular קרבנות, סמיכה is important but not essential: 'כאילו לא כפר, וכפר'. That is why it can be the difference between רבי יוחנן and רבי חנינא regarding the מילואים.
steps.confusionAlert: 'As if he did not atone' does NOT mean the קרבן failed. The last word, 'וכפר', tells you that he really did achieve atonement.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: The difference is waving
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a different practical difference, תנופה. It is essential under כל הכתוב בהן מעכב, and not essential under the other view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Waving is the difference between them. According to the one who says everything written about them is essential, it is essential. And according to the one who says that whatever is not essential for later generations is not essential for them, it is not essential.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא offers a different answer to the same question of what difference exists between the two opinions. He picks תנופה instead of סמיכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning has the same shape as רב יוסף's. תנופה is written in the מילואים, but it is not essential for regular קרבנות, so the two views split on it. The גמרא then brings a source for that, in the same pattern it used for סמיכה (steps 6–8).

steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as its proof. This first part only raises the problem with the פסוק, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links waving to atonement, but another פסוק says only blood atones. This tension is what lets the ברייתא teach that waving is not truly essential. It is built exactly like the ברייתא about סמיכה in step 3.

steps.title: רב פפא: sequestering for seven days is the difference
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the difference between the two views is פרישת שבעה. Under כל הכתוב בהן מעכב it is essential, and under the other view it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Sequestering for seven days is the difference between them. According to the one who says everything written there is essential, it is essential. According to the one who says that whatever is not essential for later generations is not essential there, it is not essential.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא offers a third practical difference between the two opinions about the מילואים. This one is the seven days that אהרן and his sons stayed apart before serving.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the מילואים, the כהנים had to stay at the entrance of the אהל מועד for seven days. If everything written there is essential, skipping that seclusion would ruin the מילואים. Under the other view it depends on whether sequestering is essential לדורות, and the גמרא is about to show it is not.

steps.title: Proof from the משנה: the backup priest is prepared, not sequestered
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says they prepare (מתקינין) a backup כהן. It does not say they sequester (מפרישין) him, so sequestering is not essential.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the משנה teaches 'they prepare' another כהן, and does not teach 'they sequester' him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from wording in our משנה. They prepare a backup כהן גדול, but the משנה never says they separate him for seven days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The backup כהן might end up doing the יום כיפור service, yet the משנה does not require him to be sequestered. If sequestering were essential, he would have to be separated too, just in case. So לדורות, sequestering is not essential.

steps.title: רבינא: seven days of garments and anointing is the difference
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says the difference is serving seven days in the extra garments (ריבוי) and with anointing (משיחה). It is essential under כל הכתוב בהן מעכב, and not essential under the other view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Seven days of the extra garments and seven days of anointing are the difference between them. According to the one who says everything written there is essential, it is essential. According to the one who says that whatever is not essential for later generations is not essential there, it is not essential.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a fourth practical difference. In the מילואים, the כהנים were dressed in the special garments and anointed for seven days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under כל הכתוב בהן מעכב, all seven days of garments and anointing are required, and missing any day ruins the מילואים. Under the other view, since the full seven days is not essential for a new כהן גדול in later generations, it is not essential in the מילואים either. As with the earlier answers, the גמרא next asks for a source that the seven days are not essential לדורות (step 13).

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the appointment works in any case
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that the words 'אשר ימשח אותו ואשר ימלא את ידו' teach that a כהן גדול is appointed even if either the garments or the anointing lasted only one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'And the כהן who is anointed and who is installed to serve in his father's place shall atone.' Why does the verse say this? Since it says 'For seven days the כהן who replaces him from his sons shall wear them,' I would only know about someone who wore the garments seven days and was anointed seven days. How do I know about someone who wore them seven days and was anointed one day, or wore them one day and was anointed seven days? The verse says 'who is anointed and who is installed': in any case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as the source. The ברייתא asks why a verse is needed, then explains that it teaches the new כהן גדול is valid even without the full seven days of both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse 'שבעת ימים ילבשם' alone might suggest you need seven of both. The extra verse about anointing and installing teaches 'מכל מקום': either one counts even if it lasted only one day. So the seven days are not מעכב לדורות.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the verse need to say this?
Wore the extra garments of the כהן גדול (ריבוי בגדים)
Was anointed with the anointing oil
In any case; whichever way it was done
Installs him; inaugurates him into service

steps.confusionAlert: Here רִיבּוּי does NOT mean the familiar method of 'including' from a verse. It means wearing the extra (eight) garments of the כהן גדול.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a ברייתא:
"And the priest who shall be anointed shall atone,
and who shall be installed
to serve in place of his father".
Why does the verse need to say this?
Since it is said:
"For seven days the priest shall wear them,
the one of his sons who replaces him",
I would know only about one who wore the extra garments seven days
and was anointed seven days.
If he wore the garments seven days and was anointed one day,

phrases.aramaic: נִתְרַבָּה יוֹם אֶחָד וְנִמְשַׁח שִׁבְעָה מִנַּיִין?
phrases.english: or wore the garments one day and was anointed seven, from where do we know?
The verse teaches:

phrases.aramaic: ״אֲשֶׁר יִמְשַׁח אוֹתוֹ וַאֲשֶׁר יְמַלֵּא אֶת יָדוֹ״ —
phrases.english: "who shall be anointed and who shall be installed":
in any case (he is appointed).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That seven days of ריבוי and משיחה are not מעכב לדורות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא on ויקרא טז:לב, 'אשר ימשח אותו ואשר ימלא את ידו': מכל מקום.

steps.title: Where is seven days of anointing required ideally?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that seven days of ריבוי לכתחילה is written explicitly, and asks where seven days of משיחה לכתחילה comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found that wearing the garments seven days is required from the start. From where do we know that anointing seven days is required from the start?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts that the seven days are not essential, but still wants a source that seven days of anointing is the ideal way. This sets up two possible answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'שבעת ימים ילבשם' directly speaks about wearing the garments seven days, so ריבוי לכתחילה is clear. Nothing explicit says anointing should be seven days. רבינא's view assumes it is required לכתחילה, so the גמרא needs a source.

keyTerms.meaning: We have found (a source for)
Ideally / from the start, even if not essential after the fact
Anointing with the holy oil

steps.confusionAlert: Keep two ideas apart: לכתחילה means 'this is how it should be done', while מעכב means 'without it, it does not work'. Seven days can be required לכתחילה and still not be מעכב.

phrases.english: We have found (a source that) wearing the garments seven days is required from the start;
anointing seven days from the start, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the source for 'not essential', asks for the source of the ideal requirement of seven days of anointing.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that seven days of משיחה is required לכתחילה.

steps.title: First answer: the verse needed to exclude it
steps.stepSummary: Since the verse was needed to teach that one day of anointing is enough after the fact, it must be that seven days is otherwise required.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: since a verse was needed to exclude it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a first answer, based on the ברייתא we just learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא needed 'מכל מקום' to allow 'נתרבה שבעה ונמשח יום אחד'. A verse would only be needed to permit one day of anointing if seven days were normally expected. So seven days of משיחה is the לכתחילה requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say (introduces one of several answers)
Since it was necessary
To exclude it / to limit it

phrases.english: If you want, say:
since the verse was needed to exclude it (so otherwise it would be required).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 using the logic of the ברייתא in step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because the verse was needed to permit fewer days, seven days of משיחה must be the ideal requirement.

steps.title: Second answer: anointing is linked to the garments
steps.stepSummary: A verse mentions anointing and installing together with the holy garments, creating a היקש: just as wearing the garments is seven days, so is anointing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say: the verse says 'And the holy garments of אהרן shall be for his sons after him, to be anointed in them and to be installed in them.' Anointing is compared to wearing the garments: just as the garments are seven days, so too anointing is seven days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, separate source from a different verse that compares anointing to wearing the garments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמות כט:כט puts 'למשחה בהם' right next to the garments and installation. This comparison (היקש) gives anointing the same rule as wearing the garments. Since wearing them is seven days לכתחילה, anointing is too.

keyTerms.meaning: It is compared (by a היקש, two things placed together in one verse)
The holy garments of the כהן גדול
Just as... so too... (form of a comparison)

steps.whatToRemember: Seven days of wearing the garments (ריבוי) and seven days of anointing (משיחה) are the ideal (לכתחילה). For later generations neither is essential (מעכב): the ברייתא says 'מכל מקום'. Seven days of משיחה comes either from the fact that the verse had to exclude it, or from a היקש to ריבוי.

phrases.english: And if you want, say: because the verse says:
"And the holy garments of Aaron
shall be for his sons after him,
to be anointed in them
and to be installed in them".
Anointing is compared to wearing the extra garments:
just as wearing the garments is seven days,
so too anointing is seven days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, independent answer to step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A היקש in שמות כט:כט links משיחה to ריבוי, so both are seven days לכתחילה.

steps.title: What is the source for the view that every detail is essential?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the view that every detail written about the מילואים is מעכב.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the one who said that everything written about them is essential?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns from the previous discussion to the reasoning behind the two views. It starts by asking where the stricter view gets its rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, two views were presented. One says every detail of the מילואים is מעכב. The other says a detail is only essential there if it is also essential for later generations. Now the גמרא wants a verse that supports the stricter view.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
The one who said (the holder of a view)
Essential; leaving it out invalidates the act
What is written about them (the מילואים)

phrases.english: What is the reason
of the one who said
everything written about them is essential?
phrases.notes: "Them" refers to the seven days of the מילואים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the earlier topic (the seven days for later generations) to the reasoning behind the dispute about the מילואים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for the view that every written detail of the מילואים is מעכב.

steps.title: The word 'so' makes every detail essential
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר ביסנא brings the verse ״וְעָשִׂיתָ לְאַהֲרֹן וּלְבָנָיו כָּכָה״. The word ״כָּכָה״ means the procedure must be done exactly as described.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר ביסנא said: The verse says, "And so shall you do to אהרן and to his sons." The word "so" teaches that the detail is essential.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק בר ביסנא answers the question with a verse. The word ״כָּכָה״ ("so," meaning "exactly like this") tells us that every detail is required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the תורה says "do it so," it means precisely in this way and no other. That word turns every detail of the פרשה into an עיכובא. If any detail is missing, the inauguration does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: So, exactly this way
An essential requirement

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the standard rule: when the תורה uses a word like ״כָּכָה״ or ״חֻקָּה,״ it makes the details essential rather than just the ideal way.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Bisna said,
the verse says:
"And so shall you do to Aaron and to his sons."
phrases.notes: This פסוק is from שמות כט:לה.

phrases.english: "So" means it is essential.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר בִּיסְנָא, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word ״כָּכָה״ in the verse makes every detail of the מילואים an עיכובא.

steps.title: Opening a challenge to this source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to challenge the source: "This works well for everything..." The rest of the challenge continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works out well for everything...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge. It first agrees that ״כָּכָה״ works for some cases. On the next amud it will point to a case the verse does not seem to cover.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״תִּינַח״ means "fine, that works." It grants part of the answer before asking about what is left. The specific gap in ״כָּכָה״ appears on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Fine, that works (it grants a point before a challenge)
Everything / all

steps.confusionAlert: ״תִּינַח״ is not agreement that ends the discussion. It means "granted, this part works... but" and always leads into a problem.

phrases.english: It works out well for all
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins testing the scope of the ״כָּכָה״ source given in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: How far the ״כָּכָה״ source from step 19 reaches.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It grants that ״כָּכָה״ covers some details, and is about to point out a detail it may not cover (completed on the next amud).
